breakfast.name: Huevos Rancheros (Ranch-Style Eggs)
breakfast.description: Fried eggs served on tortillas with spicy tomato sauce and topped with cheese and avocado
instructions: Warm tortillas in dry skillet
In separate pan, heat 1 tbsp oil
Sauté onion, garlic, and jalapeño until soft
Add crushed tomatoes, cumin, chili powder, salt, and pepper
Simmer 5-7 minutes to thicken
In another pan, heat remaining oil
Fry eggs sunny-side up or over-easy
Place one tortilla on each plate
Top with egg
Pour tomato sauce over egg
Sprinkle with cheese
Top with avocado slices
Garnish with fresh cilantro
breakfast.notes: Can be served with black beans, refried beans, or potatoes on the side
breakfast.fun_fact: Huevos Rancheros originated as a quick breakfast for ranch workers but has become iconic Mexican breakfast
stepHelp: A dry skillet (no oil) over medium heat for about 20-30 seconds per side is enough — you're just making them pliable and lightly toasted, not crisp.
About 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally. You want them soft and fragrant, not browned — lower the heat if they start to color.
The sauce is ready when a spoon dragged across the pan leaves a trail that doesn't immediately fill back in.
Sunny-side up: don't flip, cover the pan for the last minute so the top sets without flipping. Over-easy: flip once, briefly, keeping the yolk runny.

variations.title: Green Sauce Swap
variations.text: Use a roasted tomatillo salsa verde instead of the tomato sauce for a brighter, tangier version.

variations.title: Bean Layer
variations.text: Spread a layer of warm refried or black beans on the tortilla before the egg for extra heft and protein.

variations.title: Smoky Heat
variations.text: Add a chipotle in adobo to the sauce while it simmers for smoky depth instead of just jalapeño heat.

variations.title: Baked Version
variations.text: Nestle the tortillas, sauce, and eggs into a baking dish and bake at 375°F until the eggs just set for a hands-off, shareable version.

variations.title: Chorizo Boost
variations.text: Brown crumbled chorizo with the onions for a heartier, meatier plate.

serveWith.intro: A classic Mexican breakfast plate is even better with a few sides that round out the spice and richness.

items.title: Refried Beans
items.text: Creamy, savory beans are the traditional side and help balance the tomato sauce's acidity.

items.title: Mexican Rice
items.text: A scoop of tomato rice turns this into a full, hearty breakfast plate.

items.title: Fresh Fruit
items.text: Cool, juicy fruit like mango or papaya offsets the heat of the jalapeño.

items.title: Horchata
items.text: The cinnamon-rice drink's sweetness is a gentle counterpoint to the spicy sauce.

items.title: Warm Tortillas on the Side
items.text: Extra tortillas for scooping up any sauce and yolk left on the plate.

expertTips.title: Don't Skip the Simmer
expertTips.text: Give the sauce the full 5-7 minutes — a thin, watery sauce will make the tortilla soggy instead of tender.

expertTips.title: Fresh Jalapeño Matters
expertTips.text: Taste your jalapeño first; heat varies a lot. Add it gradually if you're not sure.

expertTips.title: Warm the Tortillas Last
expertTips.text: Warm tortillas right before plating so they're still pliable and warm when the sauce goes on.

expertTips.title: Runny Yolk Is the Point
expertTips.text: The yolk becomes part of the sauce when you cut into it — don't overcook the eggs.

storage.title: Fridge
storage.text: Best fresh, but sauce and toppings keep separately in an airtight container for up to 3 days — fry fresh eggs and tortillas when ready to eat.

storage.title: Freezer
storage.text: Freeze the ranchero sauce alone (without eggs or tortillas) in a sealed container for up to 2 months.

storage.title: Reheating
storage.text: Reheat sauce gently in a small saucepan over low heat, stirring occasionally, then fry fresh eggs and warm tortillas to assemble.

breakfast.makeAhead: The ranchero sauce is the perfect make-ahead component — cook it up to 3 days in advance and keep it in the fridge, or freeze it for up to 2 months. When you're ready to eat, just reheat the sauce, warm your tortillas, fry fresh eggs, and assemble.

faqs.q: Can I use flour tortillas instead of corn?
faqs.a: Yes — flour tortillas work fine and are softer, though corn tortillas are more traditional and hold up better under the sauce.

faqs.q: How do I make it less spicy?
faqs.a: Remove the jalapeño's seeds and ribs before mincing, or leave it out entirely and use a milder chili powder instead.
It already is, as written — just double check your cheese if you're avoiding animal rennet.

faqs.q: What's the best way to fry the eggs?
faqs.a: Medium-low heat with a lid on for the last minute of sunny-side-up gives you a fully set white and a runny yolk without flipping.

lunch.name: Enchiladas Verdes (Green Sauce Enchiladas)
lunch.description: Rolled tortillas filled with chicken and topped with tart green tomatillo sauce and melted cheese
instructions: Boil chicken until cooked through, shred, and set aside
For salsa verde: Boil tomatillos, jalapeños, onion, and garlic 5 minutes
Drain and blend with cilantro and salt
Stir in sour cream
Warm tortillas to make pliable
Dip tortilla in green salsa
Fill with 2 tbsp shredded chicken
Roll tightly and place seam-side down in oiled baking dish
Pour remaining salsa over enchiladas
Top with shredded cheese
Bake at 375°F for 20-25 minutes until bubbly
Garnish with more cilantro and sour cream
lunch.notes: Can be made with cheese, vegetables, or leftover cooked meat
lunch.fun_fact: The word 'enchilada' comes from 'enchilar' meaning to add chili to
alternatives: Red sauce (mole rojo) instead of green

dinner.name: Chiles Rellenos (Stuffed Peppers)
dinner.description: Roasted poblano peppers filled with cheese, battered, and fried, served in tomato sauce
instructions: Roast poblanos over flame or under broiler until charred
Place in plastic bag for 10 minutes to steam
Peel off charred skin
Make slit and carefully remove seeds
Stuff each pepper with shredded cheese
Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form
Fold in egg yolks gently
Coat stuffed peppers in flour
Dip in egg batter to coat completely
Heat oil to 350°F and fry peppers 2-3 minutes per side
Make sauce: Heat oil, sauté onion and garlic
Add tomatoes, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper
Simmer 10 minutes
Place fried peppers in sauce
Simmer 5-10 more minutes
Garnish with cilantro and serve
dinner.notes: The egg batter creates a delicate, crispy coating. Handle carefully when frying
dinner.fun_fact: Chiles Rellenos is a national dish of Mexico and represents Mexican cuisine's sophistication
alternatives: Oaxaca cheese (quesillo) instead of regular cheese
Skip batter and bake instead for lighter version

snacks.name: Tacos Al Pastor (Spit-Cooked Tacos)
snacks.description: Thin slices of marinated and cooked pork served in corn tortillas with pineapple, onion, and cilantro
instructions: Make marinade: Blend achiote paste, vinegar, garlic, cumin, chili, oregano, and oil
Marinate pork slices for 15-30 minutes
Heat cast iron skillet or griddle over high heat
Cook marinated pork in batches until edges are charred and caramelized
Build tacos: Warm tortilla, add 2-3 slices cooked pork
Top with diced pineapple, onion, and cilantro
Serve with lime wedges
Traditionally served with pineapple crown on side
snacks.notes: The achiote (annatto) gives the characteristic red color and subtle flavor
snacks.fun_fact: Tacos Al Pastor originated in Mexico City from Lebanese-Mexican fusion of shawarma technique
alternatives: Grill instead of stovetop if no cast iron
Skip achiote and use chili powder and paprika
Serve in flour tortillas for different style

desserts.name: Flan (Caramel Custard)
desserts.description: Silky smooth custard with caramel sauce. Popular dessert throughout Mexico and Latin America
instructions: Make caramel: Heat 1/2 cup sugar and water in saucepan over medium-high heat
Swirl pan occasionally until golden amber (don't stir)
Quickly pour caramel into flan dish, coating bottom and sides
In blender, combine eggs, both milks, vanilla, salt, and cinnamon
Blend until smooth
Pour custard mixture into caramel-lined dish
Place flan dish in larger roasting pan
Pour hot water into roasting pan until halfway up sides (water bath)
Bake at 350°F for 40-50 minutes
Center should jiggle slightly but not be liquid
Cool completely, then refrigerate at least 4 hours
Run knife around edges and invert onto serving plate
desserts.notes: Water bath ensures creamy custard. Don't overbake or it becomes rubbery
desserts.fun_fact: Flan is served at celebrations, quinceañeras, and special occasions throughout Mexico
alternatives: Use coconut milk instead of evaporated
Individual ramekins instead of one large flan

drinks.name: Agua Fresca (Fresh Fruit Drink)
drinks.description: Refreshing drink made from fresh fruit, water, and sugar. Popular street drink during hot Mexican afternoons
ingredients: 2 cups fresh fruit (watermelon, mango, or strawberry)
instructions: Cut fruit into chunks
Blend fruit with 1 cup water until smooth
Strain through fine mesh into pitcher
Add remaining water, sugar, and lime juice
Stir well
Chill thoroughly
Serve over ice
Garnish with fresh mint
Stir before serving
drinks.notes: Can be made with any fresh seasonal fruit
drinks.fun_fact: Agua fresca vendors are common on Mexican streets and their calls are iconic sounds of summer

drinks.name: Margarita (Tequila Cocktail)
drinks.description: Classic Mexican cocktail with tequila, lime juice, and orange liqueur, served in a salt-rimmed glass
instructions: Rub lime wedge around rim of margarita glass
Dip rim in coarse salt
Fill glass with ice
Pour tequila, lime juice, and Cointreau into shaker with ice
Shake vigorously for 10 seconds
Strain into prepared glass
Garnish with lime wheel
Serve immediately
drinks.notes: Fresh lime juice is essential for authentic taste. Simple syrup can be added for sweeter version
drinks.fun_fact: The margarita was invented in Mexico in the 1930s-40s, though its exact origins are debated
